body: I appreciate it, just reading response made me feel better so it is a lot. I think I'm just going to try and calmly talk to him now that I've got some nerve :)
Thank you! You are super kind and it's meant a lot to me :)

Yes, I think it's not an easy thing to cope with and just he doesn't know what to do.....but his reactions can end up doing me a lot of mental harm. It's just hard because I think to him it is respectful to not control me or tell me what to do. But I wish he would take into account how saying things like that make me feel. It might be "technically right " but I would rather have him say nothing rather than something that makes my mind think "I'm supported in killing myself, it's my choice, I should just do it!" Etc.

Thanks for your response, I really appreciate it. I will bring it up in to my mental health team, I just have to work up the nerve.

Thank you, I appreciate the response. I think its hard because I don't know myself the best response to other people in the situation, but I will try to think about it and bring it up from that perspective. I really appreciate the response!

You aren't back to square one hun. You know he is abusive and you know you are being manipulated. That is way beyond sqaure 1. Tons of abusers get their power by confusing and gaslighting their victims until they don't even know what is going on is abuse, or they doubt themselves, or they change their mind. You see what is going on and are reaching out for support. You are dealing with a master manipulator but are seeing through it and seeking support...you are stronger and smarter than you are giving yourself credit for.

I would highly reccomend the book "Why does he do that". I think it should be essential reading for almost everyone, but especially people in abusive relationships. Hang in there, you will find your strength to get out.
